events.ask: Why do we remember the Holocaust?

explain.say: This is one of the saddest stories in history, and we learn it so it never happens again. Between 1933 and 1945, Nazi Germany murdered six million Jewish people. This is called the Holocaust. The timeline shows, step by step, how it happened.

explain.say: It did not start with killing. It started with words and laws. Look at 1935: the Nuremberg Laws took away Jewish people's German citizenship and many of their rights. Step by step, neighbours were pushed out of everyday life. Why can small steps be so dangerous?

Roma and Sinti people, disabled people and others were also persecuted and killed. Take a breath. How does it feel to learn this?

explain.say: Allied soldiers freed the camps in 1945, and survivors shared their stories so the world would remember. Thank you for learning this with such care. Every 27 January, the day Auschwitz was freed, people everywhere remember the victims and stand up against hatred.

faq.a: The murder of about six million Jewish men, women and children by Nazi Germany and its collaborators, mostly between 1941 and 1945, after years of persecution from 1933. The Nazis also murdered Roma and Sinti people, disabled people and others.
Laws passed in Nazi Germany in 1935 that took away German citizenship from Jewish people and banned marriages between Jews and non-Jews. They made discrimination official.
asks: How did the Nazis treat Jews before the war?

faq.a: Kristallnacht, the night of broken glass, was a wave of violence against Jews on 9 and 10 November 1938. Synagogues were burned, shops and homes smashed, about 91 Jews were killed and about 30,000 Jewish men were sent to camps.
asks: What is the night of broken glass?

faq.a: Soviet troops reached Auschwitz on 27 January 1945. British, American and other Allied forces freed camps like Bergen-Belsen, Buchenwald and Dachau in April 1945, finding many survivors starving and sick.

faq.q: Why do we remember the Holocaust?
faq.a: To honour the victims, to listen to survivors, and to learn how prejudice and hatred can grow into mass murder when people stay silent. Remembering helps us protect everyone's rights today.
asks: Why is Holocaust Remembrance Day important?

facts: About six million Jewish people were murdered in the Holocaust.
Auschwitz was liberated by Soviet troops on 27 January 1945, now International Holocaust Remembrance Day.
The Nuremberg Laws were passed in September 1935.

quiz.say: About how many Jewish people were murdered in the Holocaust?
quiz.show: How many Jewish people were murdered?
quiz.why: About six million Jewish people were murdered, around two thirds of Europe's Jews.

wrong.1: The real number is about ten times higher.
wrong.2: The real number is about a hundred times higher.

quiz.say: Why is 27 January Holocaust Remembrance Day?
quiz.why: Soviet soldiers liberated Auschwitz on 27 January 1945.

wrong.1: The war in Europe began on 1 September 1939.
wrong.2: The Nuremberg Laws were passed in September 1935.
